chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, and Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Pelt during every day at the decline of the sun, and say as you said when you pelted the Jamarat al-Aqabah. So begin with the first Jamarah and pelt it from its left in the middle of the ravine, and say as you said on the day of the sacrifice.

Stand on the left of the road and face the Qiblah, then praise Allah and extol Him and send blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). Then proceed a little, so supplicate to Him and ask Him that He accepts from you. Then move forward a little, then do that at the second one, and do as you did with the first one; and pause and supplicate to Allah as you supplicated. Then go to the third, and upon you should be tranquility and dignity, so pelt, and do not pause at it.
ai.seo_question: What is the correct method and supplication for pelting the Jamarat during the days of Tashreeq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi provides the detailed jurisprudential framework for pelting the Jamarat during the days of Tashreeq, emphasizing the distinction between the first two pillars, where one pauses to supplicate, and the third, where one proceeds without stopping. It highlights the spiritual etiquette of the Hajj ritual by prescribing specific postures, facing the Qibla, and maintaining a demeanor of tranquility (sakinah) and dignity (waqar) while reciting the same phrases used at the Jamarat al-Aqaba. This practice underscores the integration of physical action with mindful devotion, reflecting the Shia emphasis on following the Imams' precise guidance in completing the Hajj rites.
